scope: Quality control, cleaning, alignment, BAM processing, count preparation, coverage tracks, and analysis-ready export only.
principle: Accuracy is prioritized over runtime and memory. AI or machine learning is favored only when validation matches the biological task and input type.

options.name: FastQC + fastp + MultiQC (recommended)
options.definition: FastQC diagnoses raw and cleaned FASTQ files, fastp performs adapter and quality filtering, and MultiQC combines all samples into one report.
pros: HTML and JSON evidence for each sample
Extends the sequencing-company fastp workflow with stronger reporting
cons: Automatic adapter detection is less controlled than supplying an exact adapter sequence
Overly aggressive filters can discard real reads
options.best_for: Most Illumina or DNBSEQ bacterial RNA-seq projects when adapter sequences are unknown.

options.name: FastQC + Cutadapt + MultiQC
options.definition: Cutadapt searches for user-specified adapter sequences and applies explicit quality and length filters; FastQC and MultiQC provide before-and-after evidence.
pros: Excellent for non-standard kits and known adapters
cons: The correct adapter sequence must be supplied
Less convenient when library chemistry is uncertain
options.best_for: Projects with exact adapter or primer sequences from the sequencing provider.

options.name: FastQC + MultiQC without trimming
options.definition: Assesses FASTQ quality but keeps the read sequences unchanged.
cons: Adapters or poor-quality tails remain if the provider did not remove them
options.best_for: FASTQ files certified as cleaned by the sequencing provider.

options.name: Bowtie2 configurable alignment (recommended)
options.definition: A gapped short-read aligner with user-selectable end-to-end or local mode, every official sensitivity preset, and expert command-line overrides. The initial setting is Bowtie2's sensitive end-to-end preset.
pros: Preset, scoring, seeding, paired-end, and reporting behavior can be adjusted in Guided tool options
cons: May reject reads with genuine damaged or untrimmed ends
Not intended for spliced eukaryotic transcripts
options.best_for: Illumina or DNBSEQ bacterial RNA-seq with a reference genome.

options.name: Bowtie2 + HISAT2 dual alignment
options.definition: Runs Bowtie2 and bacterial-mode HISAT2 independently in the same RNA-seq workflow. Both BAM/BAI sets are retained and, when gene counting is enabled, each aligner is quantified independently into a separate raw-count matrix and a separate Counts & Annotation workbook sheet.
pros: Directly compares two established short-read alignment models on the same cleaned reads
Creates separate Bowtie2 and HISAT2 BAM/BAI files
Creates separate raw-count sheets so aligner-dependent count differences remain visible
Useful for checking whether downstream conclusions are robust to aligner choice
cons: Uses approximately twice the short-read alignment compute and additional storage
The two count matrices are technical alternatives and must not be combined as biological replicates
Differences between aligners should be reviewed rather than averaged away
options.best_for: Projects that want an explicit Bowtie2-versus-HISAT2 robustness comparison while keeping both results available for downstream analysis.

options.name: Bowtie2 primary + BWA-MEM2 audit
options.definition: Runs configurable Bowtie2 as the primary alignment and configurable BWA-MEM2 independently, retaining both BAMs and a mapping-comparison report.
pros: Provides a second high-quality BAM for validation
Useful when accuracy is more important than compute cost
cons: The two BAMs must not be blindly merged
Disagreement requires locus-level review
Uses roughly twice the storage and compute
options.best_for: Accuracy-audit projects and high-value operon or DEG studies.

options.name: BWA-MEM2
options.definition: A highly optimized local gapped aligner that is also widely used for bacterial DNA-seq.
pros: Excellent compatibility with DNA-seq and variant workflows
cons: Local alignment can soft-clip read ends
Less directly interpretable than strict end-to-end mapping for transcript-boundary work
options.best_for: A confirmation alignment or projects combining RNA-seq and bacterial DNA-seq.

options.name: HISAT2 no-splice, no-softclip
options.definition: HISAT2 configured with spliced alignment disabled and soft clipping prohibited so it behaves as an unspliced bacterial mapper.
pros: Compatible with the original OpDetect preprocessing design
cons: Its main advantages target spliced genomes
Not the first accuracy choice for ordinary bacterial reference mapping
options.best_for: Reproducing an existing HISAT2-aligned study.

options.name: Use supplied FASTQ or unaligned BAM
options.definition: Skips basecalling because nucleotide calls have already been produced by the instrument or sequencing provider.
cons: Older basecalls cannot be improved without POD5
The original model and chemistry should be documented
options.best_for: Long-read FASTQ or unaligned BAM input.

options.name: Dorado SUP neural basecalling (accuracy-first)
options.definition: Oxford Nanopore Dorado decodes POD5 electrical signal with the latest chemistry-matched super-accurate neural model.
pros: Retains rich BAM tags and sequencing summaries
cons: Requires POD5 raw signal
Very compute intensive and normally benefits from an NVIDIA GPU
Dorado is installed separately under its own license
options.best_for: ONT cDNA or direct-RNA data with raw POD5 where accuracy is more important than runtime.

options.name: Dorado HAC neural basecalling
options.definition: Dorado high-accuracy neural basecalling, balancing accuracy and compute.
cons: Not the maximum-accuracy Dorado model
Requires POD5 and chemistry matching
options.best_for: Systems that cannot practically run SUP.

options.name: NanoPlot + LongQC (recommended)
options.definition: NanoPlot summarizes length, yield, and quality distributions while LongQC adds reference-free k-mer and coverage diagnostics.
pros: Detects patterns missed by short-read QC
cons: LongQC adds dependencies and runtime
Neither tool can correct a poor library
options.best_for: Accuracy-first ONT or PacBio projects.

options.name: NanoPlot
options.definition: A long-read QC report focused on read length, quality, yield, and their joint distributions.
cons: Less diagnostic depth than the combined mode
options.best_for: Routine long-read QC or systems where LongQC is unavailable.

options.name: Long-read QC without filtering
options.definition: Reports long-read quality and length but does not remove reads.
cons: Low-quality reads remain available to the aligner
options.best_for: PacBio HiFi or already filtered provider data.

options.name: Minimap2 platform-specific preset (recommended)
options.definition: Maps ONT or PacBio reads with platform-specific long-read error models and no assumption of bacterial introns.
pros: Supports ONT, PacBio CLR, and PacBio HiFi
cons: Repeat placement can remain ambiguous
A splice preset should not be used blindly for ordinary bacteria
options.best_for: Most bacterial long-read RNA-seq projects.

options.name: Minimap2 primary + Winnowmap2 repeat audit
options.definition: Runs Minimap2 as the primary map and Winnowmap2 independently to audit reads in repetitive and paralogous regions.
pros: Appropriate when compute cost is unimportant
cons: No automatic merging of conflicting placements
Most small bacterial genomes gain little outside repeats
Requires meryl
options.best_for: Repeat-rich actinomycete genomes and duplicated biosynthetic gene-cluster regions.

options.name: Winnowmap2
options.definition: A long-read mapper derived from minimap2 and optimized to reduce mapping bias in repetitive sequence.
pros: Useful for paralogs and duplicated BGC regions
cons: Adds repetitive-k-mer preprocessing
Less broadly established for bacterial transcriptomics than minimap2
options.best_for: Projects dominated by repetitive or duplicated regions.

options.name: featureCounts + optional FADU bacterial audit
options.definition: featureCounts supplies the analysis-ready integer fragment matrix. When Julia and FADU are installed, FADU additionally produces a separate fractional bacterial-overlap audit. If they are unavailable or the audit fails, the valid featureCounts export is retained and the pipeline continues with a recorded warning.
pros: Integer counts remain valid for later DESeq2 and edgeR
Optional FADU adds bacterial-specific overlap evidence when available
A missing or failed optional audit never discards the completed featureCounts matrix
cons: FADU fractional counts are not direct DESeq2 input
The optional audit requires Julia and FADU and may be skipped when they are unavailable
options.best_for: Maximum-confidence bacterial expression handoff.

options.name: featureCounts core export (recommended)
options.definition: Assigns aligned reads or fragments to normalized genomic features and exports integer raw counts.
pros: Handles paired, single, strand-specific, SAF, GFF, and long reads
Valid raw input for later DESeq2 and edgeR
cons: Conservative handling can discard ambiguous overlaps
Annotation feature and identifier fields must be correct
options.best_for: The primary later-DE count matrix.

options.name: FADU only
options.definition: A prokaryote-specific depth utility that assigns fractional evidence according to fragment overlap with unique portions of each feature.
pros: Can recover evidence for short or overlapping genes
cons: Fractional counts require care in later count-based DE
Linux or macOS and Julia dependencies
GFF3 input required
options.best_for: Secondary bacterial quantification and operon-focused handoff.

options.name: HTSeq-count
options.definition: Counts read or read-pair overlap with annotation features using explicit intersection rules.
cons: Often discards more ambiguous bacterial reads
Slower and less flexible than featureCounts
options.best_for: Reproduction or count-method sensitivity checks.

options.name: Skip counting and export BAM only
options.definition: Produces BAM, BAI, coverage, QC, metadata, and reference files but no gene-count matrix.
pros: Allows a later tool to make all counting decisions
cons: Not immediately ready for DESeq2 or edgeR
options.best_for: Users who want alignment-only handoff.

options.name: Compact CPM BigWig, strand-specific (recommended)
options.definition: Exports compact CPM-normalized BigWig tracks for IGV. A stranded library produces transcript-plus and transcript-minus tracks; an unstranded library produces one CPM track.
pros: Reduces coverage output from as many as 12 files to one or two files per sample
BigWig is indexed, compact, and efficient for IGV
CPM supports practical across-sample visual comparison
cons: Does not retain duplicate raw-depth or bedGraph copies
Incorrect library orientation inverts strand labels
options.best_for: Routine IGV inspection and clean analysis-ready export.

options.name: Comprehensive raw + CPM, BigWig + bedGraph
options.definition: Exports one-base-resolution bedGraph and BigWig tracks with raw depth and CPM-scaled signal, including forward and reverse RNA strands when the library orientation is known.
pros: Raw signal is preserved while CPM aids across-sample comparison
cons: Creates several files per sample
Incorrect library orientation inverts strand labels
options.best_for: Complete advanced-analysis handoff.

options.name: Raw unstranded BigWig only
options.definition: Exports one compact, unnormalized, unstranded BigWig depth track per sample.
cons: Cannot distinguish sense and antisense transcription
Poorer across-library comparability
options.best_for: Unstranded libraries or minimal BAM handoff.

export_contract: cleaned or newly basecalled FASTQ files when generated, plus a source-input manifest for pass-through reads
coordinate-sorted primary BAM files and BAI indexes
optional independent alternative-aligner BAM and BAI files
SAMtools flagstat, stats, and idxstats reports
raw integer gene-count matrix and per-sample assignment summaries when counting is enabled
raw and CPM BigWig or bedGraph coverage tracks
reference FASTA, FAI, normalized GFF3, SAF, and gene metadata
sample sheet and advanced-analysis metadata template
commands, parameters, tool versions, checksums, and resumable run manifest
